transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we got about 45 minutes on the calendar, Maya from Redwood here, with Ethan and Luis. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Priya Nair: Good thanks, Priya on the Helion side. We have Tomás and Anika as well. Wanted to focus on operator certification and the marketplace onramp checklist today.
[00:15] Ethan Park: Great, quick agenda — operator packaging, runbook, KMS/VPC constraints for private installs, and then the compatibility lab steps. Sound right?
[00:23] Tomás Rivera: Yep that works. Our infra is mostly k8s 1.24 with a few 1.22 clusters still in rotation, and we have some single-socket nodes for edge.
[00:34] Maya Chen: Cool — important detail. Redwood operator currently supports 1.22-1.26, but we've had some quirks around leader election timeouts on the older kubelets. We'll note that for the compatibility run.
[00:45] Anika Gupta: Quick security question, do you have an official KMS integration doc? We need to know how secrets are handled and whether keys can be customer-managed HSMs.
[00:54] Luis Ortega: Yes we do, we have a KMS integration guide — customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM are supported on Dedicated and Private deployments. For the operator we surface a secrets sidecar that fetches tokens at startup; we can document exact IAM roles.
[01:08] Priya Nair: Perfect — we'll need the exact IAM policy for our SRE team. Also, marketplace listing requires an exportable SOC2 excerpt and some telemetry expectations.
[01:18] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll share a SOC2 excerpt that's allowed for sharing, and outline telemetry endpoints. For the marketplace listing Redwood asks for: helm chart, OCI image URL, a small quickstart, support contact, and a security pack.
[01:31] Tomás Rivera: On the helm chart — do you publish to an OCI registry or deliver a tarball? We have internal policy preferring OCI manifests.
[01:39] Ethan Park: We publish to our internal OCI registry and we can provide both the chart as an OCI artifact and a packaged tarball. For Helion's marketplace, we can also give you a repo mirror so you can pull directly.
[01:50] Priya Nair: Good. Let's talk about installation modes — internal air-gapped vs VPC private. We have customers who require no egress.
[01:59] Luis Ortega: Air-gapped mode requires pre-pulled images + offline chart. We have a documented offline installation flow. For VPC/private installs, the operator needs to reach Redwood control plane endpoints for license and health checks — though we can support an enterprise option where checks are performed via a periodic signed bundle instead of persistent connectivity.
[02:17] Anika Gupta: That periodic bundle approach sounds promising, can you detail signing and audit trail? We need to present that to our compliance team.
[02:25] Maya Chen: Sure, the bundle is signed with our platform key and contains a timestamped attestation. We'll include verification steps and the audit log format. We'll add a short example to the compliance packet.
[02:35] Tomás Rivera: On constrained nodes — we want to run smaller footprint inference gateways at the edge. What's the minimum GPU/CPU and memory profile for a single replica?
[02:45] Ethan Park: For an optimized quantized model path without KV cache, a small edge shard can run on a 4 vCPU/16GB node CPU-only for embeddings and small models but for generation with low latency you typically need GPU. We can run a mini-bench: CPU-only throughput vs a T4 equivalence.
[02:59] Priya Nair: Ok please include recommended resourceRequests/limits in the chart values.yaml.
[03:05] Luis Ortega: Will do. We'll provide explicit resources and example HPA settings.
[03:12] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[03:15] Maya Chen: Back to marketplace requirements — Helion's listing will require a support SLA matrix. Do you have preferred SLAs or is it going to be variable per customer?
[03:25] Priya Nair: We'll start with Bronze/Silver/Gold tiers; the integration guide should reference how to contact Redwood support and escalation paths.
[03:33] Ethan Park: We'll prepare an SLAs doc snippet. Also include per-route telemetry that your ops teams can scrape — Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry traces, and structured logs to a configurable sink.
[03:45] Anika Gupta: About logs — PII sanitization? We cannot forward raw request payloads to Redwood in some cases.
[03:53] Maya Chen: Absolutely, we have redaction hooks. The operator can be configured to only emit metrics and structured telemetry without message bodies. For hosted marketplace listings customers can opt-in to forwarding, else we keep everything local.
[04:07] Tomás Rivera: For the compatibility run what dataset should we use? We have a demo corpus but want to make sure it's realistic for latencies.
[04:16] Ethan Park: Use a 1k sample with mixed lengths (short chat prompts, 200-token generation requests). We'll run streaming vs non-streaming to identify tail latency. We'll also simulate burst loads.
[04:28] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Who will run the lab? Helion or Redwood?
[04:33] Maya Chen: Prefer jointly — Redwood runs first on our staging to validate manifests, then Helion runs in their staging with our helm chart. We'll coordinate the kubeconfig access.
[04:43] Tomás Rivera: I'll share a limited kubeconfig for a test namespace and a list of node constraints.
[04:48] Maya Chen: Great. Add that to action items.
[04:52] Luis Ortega: A note on operator lifecycle — we recommend using our webhook-based upgrade hooks to drain replicas and warm caches during upgrades. For marketplace listing we need to show a canary rollout example.
[05:04] Anika Gupta: Can the operator run canary rollouts without external tooling? We try to minimize dependencies.
[05:10] Ethan Park: Yes, operator can orchestrate canary and A/B traffic shifting using service labels + sidecar proxies; we'll include an example with traffic percentages in the runbook.
[05:20] Priya Nair: Regarding billing and metering — marketplace expects metering labels. How does Redwood surface usage for billing?
[05:28] Maya Chen: We emit per-token counters and embedding units as metrics and we can push a billing report artifact to your S3 bucket daily. For private installs we can ship a billing aggregator that runs as a job.
[05:40] Tomás Rivera: Is there an offline aggregation mode? Some customers block outbound, so we want a local billing report to be pulled.
[05:46] Luis Ortega: Yes, offline aggregation with signed reports is supported. We'll include the schema.
[05:52] Priya Nair: Anything about licensing and entitlement checks?
[05:55] Maya Chen: We support both online license checks and offline entitlement tokens that expire. We'll include the flow diagrams.
[06:03] Ethan Park: Quick demo note — we'll send a small demo video of helm install and basic post-install smoke tests. That usually helps marketplace reviewers.
[06:12] Priya Nair: Please. Also, we need to align on support on-boarding — an initial handoff call with Helion SRE to walk the runbook.
[06:19] Maya Chen: We'll schedule that after the compatibility run.
[06:23] Tomás Rivera: One more performance ask — can you provide a quantization profile recommendation for our CPU paths? We have customers wanting smaller memory footprints.
[06:33] Ethan Park: Yes — we'll share our quant recommendation table: int8 for embeddings, FP16 or quantized int8+GPTQ for generation in edge configs, with notes on quality trade-offs. We'll attach reference evals.
[06:46] Anika Gupta: For compliance we'll need an attestation that model weights are coming from a validated supply chain. How do you handle that?
[06:54] Luis Ortega: We publish checksums of model artifacts and sign them in the build pipeline. For some enterprise partners we can provide an SBOM-like manifest.
[07:03] Priya Nair: Cool. Any blockers we anticipate for listing?
[07:08] Maya Chen: The main ones are air-gap install docs completeness, SOC2 excerpts, and a reproducible compatibility run. None are blockers, just tasks.
[07:18] Priya Nair: Good. Let's set milestones: deliver artifacts by 6/14, Redwood runs staging verification by 6/16, Helion runs compatibility by 6/18, and follow-up sync on 6/21.
[07:30] Maya Chen: Works for us. I'll recapitulate next steps in an email.
[07:35] Ethan Park: Also, for the Helm chart naming we recommend using the official pattern: com.redwood/operator-helion-<version>. We'll version semver and provide a CHANGELOG.
[07:46] Tomás Rivera: One small ask — include a simplified troubleshooting guide for common k8s errors like webhook timeouts and RBAC denied.
[07:55] Luis Ortega: Noted, we'll include a troubleshooting appendix.
[08:00] Anika Gupta: Thanks everyone. We might have a legal question about the marketplace terms but that will be a separate thread with our procurement.
[08:08] Maya Chen: Sure, we'll stand by.
[08:11] Priya Nair: That's it from Helion.
[08:13] Maya Chen: Great thanks. We'll share the artifacts and schedule the follow-up.
[08:18] [recap] Maya Chen: Action items: (1) Redwood to upload helm chart + quickstart + SOC2 excerpt, (2) Redwood to prepare runbook + quant profiles, (3) Helion to provide staging kubeconfig and node constraints. We'll target the 6/18 run.
[08:36] [end]
